title: Motion guide layer Ruffle E2E oracle: verify path-following in published SWF
description:
The authoring engine already computes path-following for guided layers (getTweenedFrame in core/src/model/timeline-query.ts calls getGuideLayerPath + samplePath, compile.ts passes scene.timeline so the guide path is read during SWF frame emit). However there is no Ruffle-backed E2E acceptance oracle to prove this actually works after publish — only authoring-canvas rendering is tested.

Scope: add apps/desktop/e2e/motion-guide.spec.ts:

1. Build a 3-layer doc at 12 fps, 5 frames:
   - Layer 0 (guide): type='guide', frame 0 keyframe with a single curved ShapeDisplayObject (a quadratic arc from (100,200) to (400,200) bending up to (250,50)).
   - Layer 1 (guided): type='guided', motion tween from frame 0 (symbol instance centered at (100,200)) to frame 4 (symbol instance centered at (400,200)). The parentFolderId / guide relationship should pair these layers (same pattern as Shell.tsx addGuideLayer).
   - Layer 2 (background): static red/blue rect so screenshots are non-blank.
2. Publish SWF via __flashTest.publish(), inject Ruffle (autoplay:on).
3. Screenshot at t~0 ms — verify guided instance is near (100, 200) (left half of stage).
4. Wait ~250 ms (~3 frames). Screenshot — verify instance is NOT near x=100 (has moved) AND is NOT on the straight horizontal path (y should deviate from 200 toward the arc peak near y=50 at x=250).
5. Wait ~400 ms. Screenshot — verify instance is near (400, 200) (right half).
6. Integrity test: same doc but with a straight (non-curved) guide path — instance should follow the straight line (y stays near 200 throughout).

Guide layer is excluded from SWF output (not rendered) — only its geometry drives the guided layer's position in each PlaceObject2.

Acceptance: motion-guide.spec.ts 2 tests pass locally with CI skip guard; confirms that compile.ts guide-path position injection produces correct per-frame PlaceObject2 matrices in Ruffle.
